title: The Businesswoman Who Believed First
script: Narrator: [thoughtful] Long before revelation reached Muhammad, Khadijah had already established herself as a formidable merchant, respected in a marketplace that rarely extended women such standing.
Narrator: She employed him to manage a trading caravan, and his conduct impressed her enough that she eventually proposed marriage herself, an unusually direct move for the era.
Narrator: [carefully] Their partnership, by most accounts, was genuinely affectionate, built on mutual respect rather than the transactional arrangements common among their contemporaries.
Narrator: Everything shifted, however, the night he returned from the cave trembling, convinced something overwhelming and possibly dangerous had just occurred to him.
Narrator: [reflective] Rather than doubting him or dismissing his fear as delusion, she wrapped him in a cloak and reassured him steadily until the trembling subsided.
Narrator: She reasoned aloud that someone so honest, so generous toward the poor, and so reliable in his dealings would never be abandoned by God to face something malevolent.
Narrator: [honestly] That reasoning wasn't naive comfort; it reflected years of firsthand observation, since she, more than anyone, understood his character intimately.
Narrator: She then consulted her cousin, a scholar familiar with earlier scriptures, who confirmed that what had occurred matched descriptions of genuine prophecy.
Narrator: [gently] From that moment, Khadijah became the first person to believe, embracing a claim that would soon cost their family considerable social and financial standing.
Narrator: During the subsequent boycott, when the clan was confined and deliberately starved of trade, she spent her own remaining wealth sustaining the besieged community.
Narrator: [calmly] If she had hesitated even briefly that first night, historians suggest the entire trajectory of those early, fragile years might have unfolded very differently.
Narrator: The Prophet reportedly never stopped praising her, even years after her death, occasionally unsettling his later wife by comparing her favorably to Khadijah's memory.
Narrator: [encouraging] Her story complicates any narrative that frames early believers as powerless outsiders, since she entered this faith from a position of genuine influence.
Narrator: Whenever generosity feels risky to me, I remember that Khadijah's wealth meant considerably less to her than the truth she'd chosen to protect.

quiz.explanation: She had already established herself as a formidable merchant, respected in a marketplace that rarely extended women such standing.

quiz.explanation: Rather than doubting him, she wrapped him in a cloak and reassured him steadily until the trembling subsided.

quiz.explanation: She reasoned that someone so honest, generous, and reliable would never be abandoned by God to face something malevolent.

quiz.explanation: During the boycott, she spent her own remaining wealth sustaining the besieged community.
